  fill(value: string, options: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<void>; // Replace the element's value with the provided text.
  filter(options: LocatorFilterOptions): PlaywrightLocator; // Narrow this locator by additional constraints.
  first(): PlaywrightLocator; // Return a locator pointing at the first matched element.
  getAttribute(name: string, options: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<null | string>; // Return an attribute value from the first matched element.
  getByLabel(text: TextMatcher, options: { exact?: boolean }): PlaywrightLocator; // Find elements by label text, scoped to this locator.
  getByPlaceholder(text: TextMatcher, options: { exact?: boolean }): PlaywrightLocator; // Find elements by placeholder text, scoped to this locator.
  getByRole(role: string, options: { exact?: boolean; name?: TextMatcher }): PlaywrightLocator; // Find elements by ARIA role, scoped to this locator.
  getByTestId(testId: string): PlaywrightLocator; // Find elements by test id, scoped to this locator.
  getByText(text: TextMatcher, options: { exact?: boolean }): PlaywrightLocator; // Find elements by text content, scoped to this locator.
  innerText(options: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<string>; // Return the rendered (visible) text of the first matched element.
  isEnabled(): Promise<boolean>; // Whether the first matched element is currently enabled.
  isVisible(): Promise<boolean>; // Whether the first matched element is currently visible.
  last(): PlaywrightLocator; // Return a locator pointing at the last matched element.
  locator(selector: string, options: LocatorLocatorOptions): PlaywrightLocator; // Create a descendant locator scoped to this locator.
  nth(index: number): PlaywrightLocator; // Return a locator pointing at the Nth matched element.
  or(locator: PlaywrightLocator): PlaywrightLocator; // Return a locator matching elements that satisfy either this locator or `locator`.
  press(value: string, options: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<void>; // Press a keyboard key while this locator is focused.
  pressSequentially(value: string, options: LocatorPressSequentiallyOptions): Promise<void>; // Focus the element and press each character in the text sequentially without clearing its existing value.
  selectOption(value: SelectOptionInput | Array<SelectOptionInput>, options: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<void>; // Select one or more options on a native `<select>` element.
  setChecked(checked: boolean, options: LocatorCheckOptions): Promise<void>; // Set a checkbox or switch-like control to a checked/unchecked state.
  textContent(options: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<null | string>; // Return the raw textContent of the first matched element (or null if missing).
  type(value: string, options: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<void>; // Type text into the element without clearing existing content.
  uncheck(options: LocatorCheckOptions): Promise<void>; // Uncheck a checkbox or switch-like control.
  waitFor(options: LocatorWaitForOptions): Promise<void>; // Wait for the element to reach a specific state.
}

interface PlaywrightDownload {
  path(options: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<null | string>; // Return the local path to the downloaded file, if available.
}

interface PlaywrightFileChooser {
  isMultiple(): boolean; // Whether the input allows selecting multiple files.
  setFiles(files: FileChooserFiles, options: { timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<void>; // Set the files for this chooser using absolute paths visible to the browser.
}

interface TabClipboardAPI {
  read(): Promise<Array<TabClipboardItem>>; // Read clipboard items, including text and binary payloads.
  readText(): Promise<string>; // Read plain text from the browser clipboard.
  write(items: Array<TabClipboardItem>): Promise<void>; // Write clipboard items.
  writeText(text: string): Promise<void>; // Write plain text to the browser clipboard.
}

interface TabDevAPI {
  logs(options: TabDevLogsOptions): Promise<Array<TabDevLogEntry>>; // Read console log messages captured for this tab.
}

interface AlertDialog {
  type: "alert";
  dismiss(): Promise<void>;
}

interface BeforeUnloadDialog {
  type: "beforeunload";
  dismiss(): Promise<void>;
}

interface ConfirmDialog {
  type: "confirm";
  accept(): Promise<void>;
  dismiss(): Promise<void>;
}

interface Documentation {
  get(name: string): Promise<string>; // Read packaged documentation by its extensionless relative path.
}

interface PromptDialog {
  type: "prompt";
  accept(text: string): Promise<void>;
  dismiss(): Promise<void>;
}

type BrowserCapabilityCollection = {
  get(id: string): Promise<unknown>;
  list(): Promise<Array<{ id: string; description: string }>>;
};

interface BrowserHistoryOptions {
  from?: string | Date; // Lower bound for visit timestamps.
  limit?: number; // Maximum number of history entries to return.
  queries?: Array<string>; // Optional terms to filter browser history with.
  to?: string | Date; // Upper bound for visit timestamps.
}

interface BrowserHistoryEntry {
  dateVisited: string; // ISO 8601 timestamp for the visit.
  title?: string; // Page title captured for the visit.
  url: string; // Visited URL.
}

interface TabInfo {
  id: string; // Metadata describing an open tab.
  providerTabId?: string; // Provider-owned identifier for matching an explicitly mentioned tab.
  title?: string;
  url?: string;
}

type TabCapabilityCollection = {
  get(id: string): Promise<unknown>;
  list(): Promise<Array<{ id: string; description: string }>>;
};

type Dialog = AlertDialog | BeforeUnloadDialog | ConfirmDialog | PromptDialog;

type ScreenshotOptions = {
  clip?: ClipRect; // Crop to a specific rectangle instead of the full viewport.
  fullPage?: boolean; // Capture the full page instead of the viewport.
};

type PlaywrightEvaluateFunction<TArg, TResult> = string | (arg: TArg) => TResult | Promise<TResult>;

type PlaywrightEvaluateOptions = {
  timeoutMs?: number; // Maximum time to spend setting up the read-only DOM scope and running the script.
};

type LoadState = "load" | "domcontentloaded" | "networkidle";

type TextMatcher = string | RegExp;

type WaitForEventOptions = {
  timeoutMs?: number;
};

type PageWaitForLoadStateOptions = {
  state?: LoadState;
  timeoutMs?: number;
};

type PageWaitForURLOptions = {
  timeoutMs?: number;
  waitUntil?: WaitUntil;
};

type LocatorCheckOptions = {
  force?: boolean;
  timeoutMs?: number;
};

type LocatorClickOptions = {
  button?: MouseButton;
  force?: boolean;
  modifiers?: Array<KeyboardModifier>;
  timeoutMs?: number;
};

type LocatorDownloadMediaOptions = {
  timeoutMs?: number; // Download timeout in milliseconds; defaults to 120000, excluding permission prompts.
};

type LocatorEvaluateFunction<TArg, TResult> = string | (element: Element, arg: TArg) => TResult | Promise<TResult>;

type LocatorEvaluateAllFunction<TArg, TResult> = string | (elements: Array<Element>, arg: TArg) => TResult | Promise<TResult>;

type LocatorFilterOptions = {
  has?: PlaywrightLocator;
  hasNot?: PlaywrightLocator;
  hasNotText?: TextMatcher;
  hasText?: TextMatcher;
  visible?: boolean;
};

type LocatorLocatorOptions = {
  has?: PlaywrightLocator;
  hasNot?: PlaywrightLocator;
  hasNotText?: TextMatcher;
  hasText?: TextMatcher;
};

type LocatorPressSequentiallyOptions = {
  timeoutMs?: number;
};

type SelectOptionInput = string | SelectOptionDescriptor;

type LocatorWaitForOptions = {
  state: WaitForState;
  timeoutMs?: number;
};

type FileChooserFiles = string | Array<string>;

type TabClipboardItem = {
  entries: Array<TabClipboardEntry>;
  presentationStyle?: "unspecified" | "inline" | "attachment";
};

interface TabDevLogsOptions {
  filter?: string; // Optional substring filter applied to the rendered log message.
  levels?: Array<"debug" | "info" | "log" | "warn" | "error" | "warning">; // Optional levels to include.
  limit?: number; // Maximum number of logs to return.
}

interface TabDevLogEntry {
  level: "debug" | "info" | "log" | "warn" | "error"; // Console log level.
  message: string; // Rendered log message text.
  timestamp: string; // ISO 8601 timestamp for when the runtime captured the log.
  url?: string; // Source URL reported by the browser runtime, when available.
}

type ClipRect = {
  height: number;
  width: number;
  x: number;
  y: number;
};

type WaitUntil = LoadState | "commit";

type MouseButton = "left" | "right" | "middle";

type KeyboardModifier = "Alt" | "Control" | "ControlOrMeta" | "Meta" | "Shift";

type SelectOptionDescriptor = {
  index?: number;
  label?: string;
  value?: string;
};

type WaitForState = "attached" | "detached" | "visible" | "hidden";

type TabClipboardEntry = {
  base64?: string;
  mimeType: string;
  text?: string;
};

---
name: entire-continuity
description: Verify live Entire session capture and checkpoint continuity at task start, after authorized commits or pushes, and at handoff in this Entire-enabled Tailor hackathon repository on Nitin's personal Mac. Exclude unrelated repositories and office machines.
---

# Entire continuity

This skill guides verification; loading it does not install or guarantee hooks. Check evidence in the actual agent session, binary and worktree. Keep live capture, historical import, local checkpoint linkage, remote ref sync and dashboard ingestion as separate findings. Aggregate Analytics is not session evidence; ignore the known Tailor Analytics discrepancy.

## Scope and authority

The maintained source is `.agents/skills/entire-continuity` in this repository. Use the copy tracked in the current checkout; older worktrees must integrate the approved source commit before expecting automatic discovery. Do not create global copies or cross-worktree symlinks.

Use existing authorization for ordinary task work. This skill alone authorizes no commits, pushes, imports, attachment, transcript uploads, scheduled checks or hidden automation. Weekly use means only an explicitly requested evidence review within this repository; it changes no approval rules and authorizes no autonomous check or schedule. Do not expand access or transmit credentials. Work only on the personal Mac; exclude StockGro and office projects.

Do not alter global Git config, authentication, hooks, trust records, permissions or credentials. Do not stop other sessions or repair dirty/diverged checkouts. Preserve checkpoint refs, original commit identities and other agents' work; never synthesize checkpoint trailers or claim retrospective live capture. Repairs need authorization for the concrete repair. Import/attach need explicit permission; attaching can amend HEAD, so permission to import is not permission to amend or force-push.

## Task-start preflight

1. Resolve the intended repository, checkout and shared Git directory with `git --no-optional-locks rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir`. Inspect `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v1 --branch`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD`, and upstream identity/divergence when present. Keep paths and SHA evidence; do not print file contents, remote URLs with embedded credentials, or full commit messages. A dirty checkout, detached HEAD, missing upstream or divergence is a finding, not permission to reset, stash, amend, fetch or switch branches. Existing upstream refs are cached evidence only.
2. Confirm Entire is already enabled from approved metadata or bounded settings inspection. If unrelated/unconfigured, report exclusion and stop this skill without enabling anything. In Tailor, inspect the existing worktree documentation when needed: `docs/entire-codex-worktrees.md` relative to the current checkout root. Never mutate that worktree or its branches as part of skill verification.
3. Run `entire version` and the actual session binary's `--version`; PATH Codex may differ from the desktop bundle. Verify syntax using installed `--help` and the matching tagged official docs. Reviewed baseline: Entire 0.11.4, desktop-bundled Codex 0.162.0-alpha.17.2, PATH Codex 0.153.4. Recheck after upgrades; the official integration tests pin Codex 0.149.0 and do not prove every newer surface works.
4. Check hook discovery, configured commands/timeouts, Git-hook wiring and trust separately from capture. Use already available status/doctor evidence or bounded approved inspection. `entire status --json` can reconcile exited sessions; `entire doctor </dev/null` is a noninteractive diagnostic, not a promise of zero state changes. Do not run either on shared live state when strict observation is required; report that diagnostic boundary instead. Never use `doctor --force`, enable/configure, run hook handlers manually, or fabricate trust hashes for verification. Review untrusted hooks through the user's Codex `/hooks` flow only when authorized.
5. Use `entire session current --json` (metadata only). Only `resolution` = `caller-env` or `ancestry` identifies the command's caller. Recent-worktree and `other-worktree` fallback are not proof of this session. Match caller ID, worktree and branch; inspect `entire session info <session-id> --json`. Require active state plus fresh lifecycle evidence from this caller during the current task before claiming live capture. An ID, installed hook file, trusted/discovered hook, old active record or historical checkpoint alone is insufficient. If freshness/source cannot be established without denied transcript access, mark live capture unverified. Never use `--transcript`, full/raw modes, denied transcript paths, or dump JSON metadata wholesale; project only safe IDs, paths, state, times, linkage and usage fields.

Conventional linked worktrees may discover the primary checkout's hook file rather than their own. Read ownership is not write ownership: compare the resolved discovered path, current-checkout path, project layer and trust. `worktree_path_not_discovered` may coexist with `ACTIVE (via root checkout)`; reconcile paths instead of blindly reinstalling. A branch lacking `.codex` can have a project-layer gap. Never copy/migrate hooks between worktrees or edit another checkout to resolve this.

## After meaningful authorized commits and pushes

Before an already-authorized commit, record original HEAD and bounded checkpoint ref identities. Let normal Git hooks perform capture; do not create a verification commit. Afterwards resolve the exact new SHA and extract only `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers (for example with Git's `%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)` format). Inspect metadata with `entire checkpoint explain --commit <exact-sha> --json` and `entire checkpoint list --session <exact-session-id> --json`; the latter is branch-scoped. Match exact commit, checkpoint and session IDs, including multi-session checkpoints. Never equate an empty branch-scoped list with deletion of all history. Missing linkage is a failure to verify, not a reason to amend the commit.

For git-refs storage, the checkpoint ref is `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last-two-ID-characters>/<id>`. Read the local ref SHA using Git; absence means local checkpoint unverified. Keep existing checkpoint refs intact, including legacy storage. Inspect selected metadata only; checkpoint trees contain private session content. Missing/null usage or incomplete child accounting is **unavailable**, not zero; report zero only if explicitly recorded.

Before an authorized push, establish the selected checkpoint destination and push_sessions setting from existing safe evidence. A normal code push can transmit transcript-derived checkpoint data; existing push authorization must cover that configured destination and content. If it does not, pause the push with the concrete missing scope. Never manually push shadow branches or change remotes/credentials. Afterwards compare each relevant local checkpoint ref SHA with the same exact ref returned by `git ls-remote --refs <approved-remote-name> <exact-ref>`; this is a remote read using existing access, not permission to authenticate anew. Bound runtime and output. If no safely established destination exists, report sync unknown. A local checkpoint, successful code push, cached origin ref or matching count alone does not prove checkpoint sync. Equal exact SHAs prove ref sync at observation time; dashboard linkage/ingestion requires separately observed session or commit view/API evidence. Don't gate this on Analytics.

## Handoff, weekly check and failures

Repeat the caller/linkage checks at handoff; an ended session with prior live evidence is valid handoff evidence, not currently active capture. Summarize repository/worktree, agent surface and binary version, session/resolution/state and freshness, original/current commit, checkpoint/local SHA, remote name/SHA and observation time, usage availability, dashboard evidence and outstanding boundary. Preserve evidence outside the repository only in an authorized location, excluding prompts and credentials.

If the surface is unsupported or capture is missing, give the exact boundary and smallest next step: e.g. discovered hooks but no caller state → an authorized fresh/resumed session in that worktree with reviewed hooks, then metadata verification. Continue authorized coding if appropriate, clearly marking capture unverified. Never relabel an import as live. For requested historical recovery, first inspect `entire import --help`, the agent-specific import help, and `entire session attach --help`; explain local-history versus commit-linkage effects and request the exact missing mutation permission before execution. No automatic amend, force, upload or live test commit.

Optional repeatability helper: `python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/classify_evidence.py <sanitized-evidence.json>`. Read its short input contract before use. It classifies manually normalized evidence, does not collect/verify facts, and performs no Git, Entire, network or transcript operations. Unknown facts stay unknown. For an explicitly requested weekly evidence review, invoke this skill and sample the week's exact authorized commits and checkpoints within the selected repository; report coverage limits, not universal completeness.

## Sources and known evidence

Use the [Entire 0.11.4 Codex integration contract](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/v0.11.4/cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/AGENT.md) for discovery/trust caveats and the [0.11.4 storage and remote reference](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/v0.11.4/README.md#checkpoint-remote) for sync behavior. Installed help governs executable syntax.

User-reported baseline, not this skill's new live test: bundled-CLI session `01a1287f-9b41-7ce2-86f4-d9384c3f8718`, checkpoint `01M4M835G024JZH0PJPA615GFB`, commit `381b750db363e4ff403cfdd3ac722455da00addb` on `codex/verify-entire-capture`; local/remote checkpoint SHA `6e35f68e8211412362beb43593473d950a03730b`. Eleven refs reportedly matched origin and dashboard commit linkage was observed. Session usage agreed across metadata/API/session view. Desktop UI live capture was not separately tested. Do not extrapolate these facts to the current session or investigate Analytics.

name: entire-continuity
description: Verify live Entire session capture and checkpoint continuity at task start, after authorized commits or pushes, and at handoff in this Entire-enabled Tailor hackathon repository on Nitin's personal Mac. Exclude unrelated repositories and office machines.
---

# Entire continuity

This skill guides verification; loading it does not install or guarantee hooks. Check evidence in the actual agent session, binary and worktree. Keep live capture, historical import, local checkpoint linkage, remote ref sync and dashboard ingestion as separate findings. Aggregate Analytics is not session evidence; ignore the known Tailor Analytics discrepancy.

## Scope and authority

The maintained source is `.agents/skills/entire-continuity` in this repository. Use the copy tracked in the current checkout; older worktrees must integrate the approved source commit before expecting automatic discovery. Do not create global copies or cross-worktree symlinks.

Use existing authorization for ordinary task work. This skill alone authorizes no commits, pushes, imports, attachment, transcript uploads, scheduled checks or hidden automation. Weekly use means only an explicitly requested evidence review within this repository; it changes no approval rules and authorizes no autonomous check or schedule. Do not expand access or transmit credentials. Work only on the personal Mac; exclude StockGro and office projects.

Do not alter global Git config, authentication, hooks, trust records, permissions or credentials. Do not stop other sessions or repair dirty/diverged checkouts. Preserve checkpoint refs, original commit identities and other agents' work; never synthesize checkpoint trailers or claim retrospective live capture. Repairs need authorization for the concrete repair. Import/attach need explicit permission; attaching can amend HEAD, so permission to import is not permission to amend or force-push.

## Task-start preflight

1. Resolve the intended repository, checkout and shared Git directory with `git --no-optional-locks rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir`. Inspect `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v1 --branch`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD`, and upstream identity/divergence when present. Keep paths and SHA evidence; do not print file contents, remote URLs with embedded credentials, or full commit messages. A dirty checkout, detached HEAD, missing upstream or divergence is a finding, not permission to reset, stash, amend, fetch or switch branches. Existing upstream refs are cached evidence only.
2. Confirm Entire is already enabled from approved metadata or bounded settings inspection. If unrelated/unconfigured, report exclusion and stop this skill without enabling anything. In Tailor, inspect the existing worktree documentation when needed: `docs/entire-codex-worktrees.md` relative to the current checkout root. Never mutate that worktree or its branches as part of skill verification.
3. Run `entire version` and the actual session binary's `--version`; PATH Codex may differ from the desktop bundle. Verify syntax using installed `--help` and the matching tagged official docs. Reviewed baseline: Entire 0.11.4, desktop-bundled Codex 0.162.0-alpha.17.2, PATH Codex 0.153.4. Recheck after upgrades; the official integration tests pin Codex 0.149.0 and do not prove every newer surface works.
4. Check hook discovery, configured commands/timeouts, Git-hook wiring and trust separately from capture. Use already available status/doctor evidence or bounded approved inspection. `entire status --json` can reconcile exited sessions; `entire doctor </dev/null` is a noninteractive diagnostic, not a promise of zero state changes. Do not run either on shared live state when strict observation is required; report that diagnostic boundary instead. Never use `doctor --force`, enable/configure, run hook handlers manually, or fabricate trust hashes for verification. Review untrusted hooks through the user's Codex `/hooks` flow only when authorized.
5. Use `entire session current --json` (metadata only). Only `resolution` = `caller-env` or `ancestry` identifies the command's caller. Recent-worktree and `other-worktree` fallback are not proof of this session. Match caller ID, worktree and branch; inspect `entire session info <session-id> --json`. Require active state plus fresh lifecycle evidence from this caller during the current task before claiming live capture. An ID, installed hook file, trusted/discovered hook, old active record or historical checkpoint alone is insufficient. If freshness/source cannot be established without denied transcript access, mark live capture unverified. Never use `--transcript`, full/raw modes, denied transcript paths, or dump JSON metadata wholesale; project only safe IDs, paths, state, times, linkage and usage fields.

Conventional linked worktrees may discover the primary checkout's hook file rather than their own. Read ownership is not write ownership: compare the resolved discovered path, current-checkout path, project layer and trust. `worktree_path_not_discovered` may coexist with `ACTIVE (via root checkout)`; reconcile paths instead of blindly reinstalling. A branch lacking `.codex` can have a project-layer gap. Never copy/migrate hooks between worktrees or edit another checkout to resolve this.

## After meaningful authorized commits and pushes

Before an already-authorized commit, record original HEAD and bounded checkpoint ref identities. Let normal Git hooks perform capture; do not create a verification commit. Afterwards resolve the exact new SHA and extract only `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers (for example with Git's `%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)` format). Inspect metadata with `entire checkpoint explain --commit <exact-sha> --json` and `entire checkpoint list --session <exact-session-id> --json`; the latter is branch-scoped. Match exact commit, checkpoint and session IDs, including multi-session checkpoints. Never equate an empty branch-scoped list with deletion of all history. Missing linkage is a failure to verify, not a reason to amend the commit.

For git-refs storage, the checkpoint ref is `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last-two-ID-characters>/<id>`. Read the local ref SHA using Git; absence means local checkpoint unverified. Keep existing checkpoint refs intact, including legacy storage. Inspect selected metadata only; checkpoint trees contain private session content. Missing/null usage or incomplete child accounting is **unavailable**, not zero; report zero only if explicitly recorded.

Before an authorized push, establish the selected checkpoint destination and push_sessions setting from existing safe evidence. A normal code push can transmit transcript-derived checkpoint data; existing push authorization must cover that configured destination and content. If it does not, pause the push with the concrete missing scope. Never manually push shadow branches or change remotes/credentials. Afterwards compare each relevant local checkpoint ref SHA with the same exact ref returned by `git ls-remote --refs <approved-remote-name> <exact-ref>`; this is a remote read using existing access, not permission to authenticate anew. Bound runtime and output. If no safely established destination exists, report sync unknown. A local checkpoint, successful code push, cached origin ref or matching count alone does not prove checkpoint sync. Equal exact SHAs prove ref sync at observation time; dashboard linkage/ingestion requires separately observed session or commit view/API evidence. Don't gate this on Analytics.

## Handoff, weekly check and failures

Repeat the caller/linkage checks at handoff; an ended session with prior live evidence is valid handoff evidence, not currently active capture. Summarize repository/worktree, agent surface and binary version, session/resolution/state and freshness, original/current commit, checkpoint/local SHA, remote name/SHA and observation time, usage availability, dashboard evidence and outstanding boundary. Preserve evidence outside the repository only in an authorized location, excluding prompts and credentials.

If the surface is unsupported or capture is missing, give the exact boundary and smallest next step: e.g. discovered hooks but no caller state → an authorized fresh/resumed session in that worktree with reviewed hooks, then metadata verification. Continue authorized coding if appropriate, clearly marking capture unverified. Never relabel an import as live. For requested historical recovery, first inspect `entire import --help`, the agent-specific import help, and `entire session attach --help`; explain local-history versus commit-linkage effects and request the exact missing mutation permission before execution. No automatic amend, force, upload or live test commit.

Optional repeatability helper: `python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/classify_evidence.py <sanitized-evidence.json>`. Read its short input contract before use. It classifies manually normalized evidence, does not collect/verify facts, and performs no Git, Entire, network or transcript operations. Unknown facts stay unknown. For an explicitly requested weekly evidence review, invoke this skill and sample the week's exact authorized commits and checkpoints within the selected repository; report coverage limits, not universal completeness.

## Sources and known evidence

Use the [Entire 0.11.4 Codex integration contract](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/v0.11.4/cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/AGENT.md) for discovery/trust caveats and the [0.11.4 storage and remote reference](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/v0.11.4/README.md#checkpoint-remote) for sync behavior. Eleven refs reportedly matched origin and dashboard commit linkage was observed. Session usage agreed across metadata/API/session view. Desktop UI live capture was not separately tested. Do not extrapolate these facts to the current session or investigate Analytics.

# NIT-265 reference and verification

Reference inspected read-only in Comet on Nitin's personal Mac, 11 October 2026. Public https://neatlogs.com and authenticated Tailor Demo Sandbox trace list, recovered/exhausted detail, errors, graph, timeline, tag search, no-match search and latency filter. No JS injection, response interception, ingestion, model calls or real-account changes. The retained six original preflight references and four later safe crops are outside the repository in the dated Codex visualization review folder for session `01a128b8-8734-7721-9f61-4697417b9557`.

Native reference window was 3440×1410, browser content crop 3430×1318; app-safe crops additionally omit the left account rail. Comet showed 110% zoom. Replica desktop capture uses 3127×1204 CSS pixels, approximately corresponding to that scale; comparison images normalize the reference raster to this frame and explicitly label normalization. This is visual comparison evidence, not independently measured identical CSS viewports or pixel parity. Replica mobile checks use 390×844; a real responsive mobile reference was not inspected. Loading was transient during native navigation; a persistent real backend failure was not induced. Local loading/failure/interruption states are tested separately.

## Observed semantics and structure

- Public: cyan hackathon strip, sparse top navigation, gray first hero sentence above heavy black second sentence, silver San Francisco bridge/city/fog scene, dark setup button and outlined entry CTA.
- App: narrow pale icon rail, Traces title/tabs and right search/date/refresh controls, capsule filters, daily histogram, dense table, bottom row count/pagination. Columns: selection, Ingested at, Status, Detections, Evals, Input, Output, Comments, Replay.
- Trace: timestamp/back toolbar; navigator, graph/timeline toggles; right-aligned input bubble over centered expandable parent-linked steps; root output below. Graph occupies the right pane. Timeline occupies a horizontal bottom pane, gray successful bars and red errors. Native graph selection highlighted a node/row without opening inline detail; inline span expansion displayed I/O/error/attributes.
- Ready indicates processing, not final task success. The 43ms recovered reference has one ERROR child and no Execution Failed detection. The exhausted 50ms header/51ms root reference has two ERROR children and two detections; root output safely escalates. Replica avoids that header/root rounding difference by deriving all durations from the same record.
- Source tagged list showed 10 baseline traces. Search `timeout-recovered` settled at 2 matching rows with span match chips; `zz-no-fictional-trace` showed “No traces found / Try adjusting your filters or date range.” Latency greater than .045 seconds showed 2 exhausted rows. Counts change with filtering. Optional expansion failures and Analytics were not investigated.

## Bounded differences for review

- Landing reproduces the first-screen composition only, not the full scrolling marketing site. Entry CTA replaces Start free; other marketing links and setup action explicitly announce unavailable scope. Static sourced photographic assets replace the real site's animated layered atmosphere; no motion parity claim.
- Synthetic/session/version notice is added. There are two controlled order lookup fixtures, not the source catalogue/refund flow. Saved project text never drives fixtures; IDs are session-scoped stable UUID-derived records.
- Relevant fixture/detection/tag/search/latency controls work; session/user/workflow/eval/metadata/advanced filtering, date selection, display menus and broader app routes are outside scope. Capsule filters are native selectors rather than the incumbent's popover editor. Search uses substring rather than ranked matching/span chips. Evals/comments columns are empty; no evaluation is fabricated.
- Navigator is a two-trace selector rather than paged reference tabs. Graph preserves root/child relationships in a fixed right pane rather than draggable canvas/splitters. Selection opens the corresponding inline span and marks it; direct links use `?span=`. Timeline has explicit duration labels and is derived from coherent offsets. No live replay, comments, assistant or side effects are offered.
- Typography/spacing/icon drawings are hand-reconstructed from observation using sourced Geist. Dense tables scroll horizontally on mobile; other content fits 390px. Dark theme is local and approximate, not reference-certified.

## Assets and implementation boundaries

`public/assets/landscape.webp` and `portrait.webp` were fetched 11 October from the public Neatlogs `/hero-silver/mobile-scene-landscape-v1.webp` and `/hero-silver/mobile-scene-portrait-v1.webp`; `geist.woff2` is the public site's Geist font asset. Used only for this local review replica, not a claim of redistribution/licensing or deployment permission. No authenticated cookies/assets were fetched by scripts. Frontend/runtime requests stay local. Node HTTP, native SQLite and strict TypeScript avoid an application framework for this small two-fixture slice; Playwright is development-only.

Existing SDK setup tests and network-free Doctor pass. Real Tailor→Neatlogs execution telemetry remains configured separately and unmodified; authenticated telemetry health was not newly verified. Local synthetic replica data is not proof of that ingestion.

{"id":"NIT-265","uuid":"8224e439-786b-483c-9970-039dec60898d","title":"Build faithful Neatlogs replica and APIs","description":"## Agreed scope; ready for independent implementation

**Decision recorded 11 October 2026:** build a basic buyer-led Tailor proof of concept. Tailor is intended for software companies; Neatlogs is the first example. This ticket is the complete first build slice, including reference inspection, data contracts, developer harness and verification. The bounded replica scope is settled and ready for implementation when Nitin launches the coding session. <issue id="193a97a8-bd29-45e5-bfba-dd1d7c790ca8" href="https://linear.app/nitinkhanna/issue/NIT-253/review-proof-plan-and-decide-next-step">NIT-253</issue> can run in parallel and does not need to be completed before this ticket starts. This Linear correction launches no coding session and is not a commitment to the full commercial product.

## Outcome and scope

A visitor starts on a faithful limited replica of the current Neatlogs public landing page, opens a Tailor entry CTA (proposed label: “Try with your project”), describes an existing/planned project, then freely explores the supported synthetic demo. Save that description and the demo state during and after the visit so the vendor can inspect the session. For this slice, use two clearly labelled deterministic fixtures. **Saving text does not generate personalization; no LLM or agent exists in this slice.** Make that limitation explicit in the UI.

Included:

* Public landing/entry flow; app shell matching the current real Neatlogs product.
* Trace list and trace detail, including span tree, timeline, inputs/outputs, errors and timing.
* Relevant search/filters for this trace workflow, with truthful counts and empty states.
* List → detail → Back/Forward, direct trace/span links and reload.
* Basic typed APIs, one persistent canonical dataset per session, and a developer-only fixture/validation harness.
* Minimal developer/vendor inspection of saved input and scenario state. A full vendor dashboard and full authentication are outside scope; use fictional/local sessions until access and retention are agreed.

**Visual fidelity to actual current Neatlogs is a dealbreaker.** Do not invent a generic observability dashboard or use the older approximate Paper designs as design truth.

## Inputs and reference inspection

Repository: [https://github.com/nitink133/tailor-neathack](<https://github.com/nitink133/tailor-neathack>)
Parallel agent discussion and post-replica review: [NIT-253](<https://linear.app/nitinkhanna/issue/NIT-253>)
Setup evidence: [NIT-252](<https://linear.app/nitinkhanna/issue/NIT-252>)
Sandbox catalogue: [https://chatgpt.com/space/page_3bf8c65eb9248191b298a09646a631d6](<https://chatgpt.com/space/page_3bf8c65eb9248191b298a09646a631d6>)
Background workshop: [https://chatgpt.com/space/page_a57ae2efb9808191ab50b99c369d35cf](<https://chatgpt.com/space/page_a57ae2efb9808191ab50b99c369d35cf>)
Public design: [https://neatlogs.com/](<https://neatlogs.com/>)
Read-only authenticated sandbox: [https://app.neatlogs.com/traces?orgId=8186e5df-b745-4e66-a01d-94c420459c43&projectId=a35a7334-258e-441c-b2e1-b8198a263f21&f=tags\~tailor-demo-20261010-v1](<https://app.neatlogs.com/traces?orgId=8186e5df-b745-4e66-a01d-94c420459c43&projectId=a35a7334-258e-441c-b2e1-b8198a263f21&f=tags~tailor-demo-20261010-v1>)

The workshop and [historical runtime research](<https://linear.app/nitinkhanna/issue/NIT-268>) predate the selected replica direction. Follow this ticket when they conflict.

Before UI implementation, inspect the public landing and logged-in Tailor Demo Sandbox using **Nitin's personal Mac / Comet**, read-only. Capture safe screenshots and behavior notes for the included surfaces, including layout, typography, spacing, controls, status semantics, selected-span behavior, navigation, loading/error/empty states and representative filter results. Label reference dates/viewports. Discover the exact fields and controls within the agreed surfaces through this read-only inspection; that detail discovery is implementation work, not a new product-scope approval gate. No real-account changes, injection or re-ingestion. If the reference browser is inaccessible, report the exact blocker and continue independent contract work; do not substitute guessed UI. Confirm trace outcome versus child-error badges from observed behavior.

The existing sandbox's 10 traces / 47 spans / 9 sessions and 40 saved manual rubric answers are reference/teaching evidence only. Four optional expansion cases remain unresolved (two Processing failed, two not found, cause unknown). That expansion and the parked Analytics discrepancy do not block a controlled replica.

## Repository and Entire preflight

* Inspect the current repository, its README/package scripts, root AGENTS.md and relevant .agents/skills. Fetch origin/main, record its actual SHA, and use a **new feature branch and separate worktree from that freshly fetched main**.
* Last verified main supplied by the setup session: **9ba9a45f6d8fa916a56bcee31738ba57cc7e2b99**. It includes consolidated work, a relative AGENTS.md and project-local .agents/skills/entire-continuity. Verify rather than assume it is still latest.
* The primary local checkout was dirty/stale. Do not reset, clean, overwrite, switch or reuse it. Preserve human/other-agent work and all existing refs.
* Before each actual implementing session, follow the project-local Entire continuity skill and verify the live capture state for that exact session/branch. Healthy instructions/hooks alone are insufficient. Historical live CLI capture is proven; desktop UI capture remains untested. If capture cannot be verified, stop implementation and report.
* Historical genuine checkpoint: **01M4M9KRQN7RM3S5SK606GSN8Q**; corresponding local/remote checkpoint-ref SHA **d15aeacf52215aff94ec4a887ba951652d254646**. These prove earlier capture, not this next session. Never fabricate a checkpoint or transcript.
* Preserve the existing **real Tailor → Neatlogs observability integration**. The synthetic Neatlogs replica UI is demo content; it is a separate concern from real telemetry about Tailor execution.

## API and data contract

Keep implementation small and reuse appropriate existing code after inspection. Do not prescribe a new framework without evidence. Define typed request/response and error contracts before the UI consumes them.

One canonical session dataset must support:

* Creation/readback of a demo session with saved visitor input and immutable session ownership/boundary.
* Read/query projections for trace list and filters, trace detail, span tree/timeline and I/O/errors/timing.
* Versioned scenario state and a developer-only operation for selecting/proposing a supported fixture.
* Deterministic validation, atomic publication and actual readback of the accepted version; stale, invalid or partial updates leave the previous good version intact.
* Stable trace/span/session IDs; valid parent relationships; consistent timings and status semantics; no cross-session data exposure.
* Persistence across navigation, reload and server restart, sufficient for later vendor review. Document where data lives and how the local test dataset can be reset; no real buyer-data collection, public exposure or indefinite-retention promise.
* Clear unknown-ID, unsupported-action, empty, loading and failure responses. Browser and API must agree on active scenario/version.

The developer harness uses the same APIs/contracts as the UI. It may choose deterministic fixtures, validate intentionally broken changes and inspect saved sessions. It must not pretend to interpret arbitrary project descriptions.

## Two fixtures

1. **Order lookup: first attempt fails, retry recovers.** The span tree shows failure and recovery; the final answer is correct for the fictional order.
2. **Order lookup: both attempts fail.** Both failures, timings and final output agree; the agent safely escalates without inventing order data or claiming it contacted a real person.

Both are clearly synthetic. They use coherent linked records across every included view. Distinguish final task outcome from trace/child error indicators using observed Neatlogs semantics.

## Acceptance and run evidence

- [ ] Dated current-product reference screenshots and behavior/contract notes cover every included surface.
- [ ] Side-by-side screenshots at matching viewports show faithful layout, type, controls and data hierarchy; every material deviation is listed for Nitin.
- [ ] Both fixtures pass the same API/UI consistency checks. List counts, filters, trace IDs, span parents, timeline, input/output and final outcome agree.
- [ ] A deliberately invalid/stale proposal is rejected without partial changes; a corrected update is atomically accepted and verified by independent readback.
- [ ] Two fictional sessions remain isolated through API reads/updates and direct links. Neither can read or overwrite the other.
- [ ] Back/Forward, direct links, reload, restart, repeated clicks and interrupted requests keep coherent state; unknown/unsupported actions fail honestly.
- [ ] Visitor input and accepted state remain available for authorized local vendor/developer inspection after exploration.
- [ ] Existing real observability/tests still work. No real account mutations, frontend credentials, model calls/spend or deployment.
- [ ] Inspect and document the actual install/dev/API/fixture/reset/test/typecheck/lint/build commands in README or the repo's established runbook. Run all applicable repository checks on the final code; list passed, failed and not-run checks separately. Do not invent script names.
- [ ] Return branch/base/final commit, changed files, run instructions, screenshots, fixture/validation evidence, real telemetry references where available, genuine session/checkpoint evidence and remaining limitations.

## Non-goals and stop point

No browser JavaScript injection or response interception in the real Neatlogs account. No Analytics, Evals, built-in assistant, billing, full auth, calendar/audio, automatic product onboarding, multi-vendor platform or commercial naming work. Do not run model inference, claim arbitrary personalization, deploy, change sharing, push/merge or contact anyone merely because this ticket exists.

Stop for Nitin's review in [NIT-253](<https://linear.app/nitinkhanna/issue/NIT-253>) after the deterministic replica/API proof. The later bounded agent loop is [NIT-269](<https://linear.app/nitinkhanna/issue/NIT-269>), conditional on evidence and separate approval. The application uses a dense gray-and-white workspace: a narrow icon rail, compact controls, fine dividers, small labels, tabular data and restrained status colors. Trace details preserve the input, steps and output hierarchy, with an optional right graph and bottom timeline.
DESIGN.md:122:Green Ready marks processing status; it does not establish a successful task outcome. Red ERROR text, a pale red error block and Execution Failed capsules communicate separate span and detection states. Timeline bars use neutral gray for normal spans and red for error spans. DESIGN.md:124:The local `.dark` theme swaps app surface, divider, text and status variables. It also uses dark failure, error and selected-span fills. It is approximate and has no certified incumbent dark-theme parity; the public landing retains its silver, light palette.
DESIGN.md:126:## Typography
DESIGN.md:130:The final desktop hero uses an 80px, weight-650 main sentence, with a 58px, weight-600 gray first sentence, 1.12 line height and tight tracking. At 900px and below these become 46px and 38px; at 600px and below they become 36px and 31px, with 1.15 line height. The wordmark is 28px, reducing to 23px on mobile.
DESIGN.md:140:Detail structure is a timestamp/back toolbar, trace selector and graph/timeline toggles, a right-aligned input bubble, centered steps and root output. The flow column is at most 650px. The optional graph reserves the right 38% of the canvas and draws a fixed parent/child tree. At 900px and below it becomes a block above the flow. The optional timeline remains a horizontal bottom section, with 160px label and 65px duration columns on desktop, reducing to 110px and 40px on mobile. Bars derive position and width from span offsets and durations.
DESIGN.md:146:The interface has no box-shadow vocabulary. Depth comes from near-white surfaces, one-pixel dividers and borders, selected fills and nested span connectors. The public photograph supplies atmospheric depth. The toast is fixed above content with a charcoal fill; it does not introduce a floating card system. No motion parity is implemented; the hero is static rather than the incumbent's animated layered atmosphere.
DESIGN.md:150:Controls and graph roots use 6px corners, JSON blocks 7px, fields and notes 8px, solid CTAs 9px, bubbles and outlined hero actions 10px, and the steps container 12px. Filters, detections and graph children use 20px capsule corners. Most borders are one pixel in the shared divider color. Parent-child span relationships are explicit lines and indentation, with tighter indentation on mobile. Icons are reconstructed 16px outline SVGs, with reduced sizes in compact span rows.
DESIGN.md:156:**Forms and filtering.** Entry uses a visibly labeled, required textarea, a native radio fieldset and a submit action that disables while saving and restores after failure. Errors appear in a `role="alert"` paragraph. Search, fixture, detection, tag and minimum latency controls use native inputs/selectors inside compact bordered capsules; they are not the incumbent's popover editor. Empty results show “No traces found,” explanatory text and a clear-filters action.
DESIGN.md:158:**Trace table.** Keep the incumbent column order: selection, Ingested at, Status, Detections, Evals, Input, Output, Comments and Replay. Use ellipsis for dense row values and retain horizontal scrolling. Evals/comments stay empty; replay reports unavailable scope. Ready retains its screen-reader text and explanatory title. Footer counts follow the filtered rows.
DESIGN.md:160:**Inline spans, graph and timeline.** Span buttons expose `aria-expanded`, rotate their disclosure icon and reveal INPUT plus OUTPUT or ERROR JSON, timing and parent metadata, copy and direct-link actions. Selected spans use the blue-tinted fill. Errors have textual labels and bordered red blocks. The graph and timeline are optional toggles with `aria-pressed`; selecting their links opens the corresponding inline span using `?span=`. The graph is fixed and cannot be dragged or resized. The timeline has textual duration labels alongside its colored bars.
DESIGN.md:168:- Do keep span detail inline, graph on the desktop right and timeline on the bottom; preserve the responsive graph placement and horizontal table scrolling.
DESIGN.md:172:- Don't treat the two-trace navigator, fixed graph, substring search or native capsule selectors as full incumbent feature parity.

# AGENTS.md

Tailor is a neatHack (October 2026) candidate. No application features yet.

## Setup

- Node >= 26.7.0, npm >= 11.19.0. Install with `npm ci`.
- `npm run typecheck` — `tsc --noEmit`.
- `npm test` — Node's built-in test runner (`node --test`, native TypeScript stripping).
- `npm run doctor:local` — Neatlogs SDK Doctor, local mode (network-free, deliberately does not load `.env.local`).
- `npm run doctor:probe` — authenticated Doctor probe; loads `.env.local`.
- `npm run smoke:trace` — sends one SYNTHETIC trace (no model calls) and reads it back by ID; loads `.env.local`. Each run creates a trace in the Neatlogs project.
- `npm run env:check` — reports only whether `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set, never its value.

## Local secrets

- Put secrets in `.env.local` (gitignored, `chmod 600`). Scripts that need them run `node --env-file-if-exists=.env.local …` directly; Node rejects `--env-file*` in `NODE_OPTIONS`, so `npm exec` cannot pass it to the CLI.
- Shell-exported variables take precedence over `.env.local`.
- Never `cat`, read, print, or log `.env.local` or the key; use `npm run env:check`.

## Rules

- Secrets live only in the environment or a gitignored `.env.local`; `.env.example` holds placeholders. Never print, log, or commit `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`.
- `neatlogs` is pinned to an exact version; upgrade deliberately, never downgrade.
- Do not run `neatlogs doctor --probe` until the Neatlogs project and region are confirmed and the key is set.
- Entire captures Cursor sessions via `.cursor/hooks.json` and git hooks; keep `.entire/settings.json` and `.cursor/hooks.json` tracked and preserve unrelated hooks.

# Entire continuity

This skill guides verification; loading it does not install or guarantee hooks. Check evidence in the actual agent session, binary and worktree. Keep live capture, historical import, local checkpoint linkage, remote ref sync and dashboard ingestion as separate findings. Aggregate Analytics is not session evidence; ignore the known Tailor Analytics discrepancy.

## Scope and authority

The maintained source is `.agents/skills/entire-continuity` in this repository. Use the copy tracked in the current checkout; older worktrees must integrate the approved source commit before expecting automatic discovery. Do not create global copies or cross-worktree symlinks.

Use existing authorization for ordinary task work. This skill alone authorizes no commits, pushes, imports, attachment, transcript uploads, scheduled checks or hidden automation. Weekly use means only an explicitly requested evidence review within this repository; it changes no approval rules and authorizes no autonomous check or schedule. Do not expand access or transmit credentials. Work only on the personal Mac; exclude StockGro and office projects.

Do not alter global Git config, authentication, hooks, trust records, permissions or credentials. Do not stop other sessions or repair dirty/diverged checkouts. Preserve checkpoint refs, original commit identities and other agents' work; never synthesize checkpoint trailers or claim retrospective live capture. Repairs need authorization for the concrete repair. Import/attach need explicit permission; attaching can amend HEAD, so permission to import is not permission to amend or force-push.

## Task-start preflight

1. Resolve the intended repository, checkout and shared Git directory with `git --no-optional-locks rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir`. Inspect `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v1 --branch`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD`, and upstream identity/divergence when present. Keep paths and SHA evidence; do not print file contents, remote URLs with embedded credentials, or full commit messages. A dirty checkout, detached HEAD, missing upstream or divergence is a finding, not permission to reset, stash, amend, fetch or switch branches. Existing upstream refs are cached evidence only.
2. Confirm Entire is already enabled from approved metadata or bounded settings inspection. If unrelated/unconfigured, report exclusion and stop this skill without enabling anything. In Tailor, inspect the existing worktree documentation when needed: `docs/entire-codex-worktrees.md` relative to the current checkout root. Never mutate that worktree or its branches as part of skill verification.
3. Run `entire version` and the actual session binary's `--version`; PATH Codex may differ from the desktop bundle. Verify syntax using installed `--help` and the matching tagged official docs. Reviewed baseline: Entire 0.11.4, desktop-bundled Codex 0.162.0-alpha.17.2, PATH Codex 0.153.4. Recheck after upgrades; the official integration tests pin Codex 0.149.0 and do not prove every newer surface works.
4. Check hook discovery, configured commands/timeouts, Git-hook wiring and trust separately from capture. Use already available status/doctor evidence or bounded approved inspection. `entire status --json` can reconcile exited sessions; `entire doctor </dev/null` is a noninteractive diagnostic, not a promise of zero state changes. Do not run either on shared live state when strict observation is required; report that diagnostic boundary instead. Never use `doctor --force`, enable/configure, run hook handlers manually, or fabricate trust hashes for verification. Review untrusted hooks through the user's Codex `/hooks` flow only when authorized.
5. Use `entire session current --json` (metadata only). Only `resolution` = `caller-env` or `ancestry` identifies the command's caller. Recent-worktree and `other-worktree` fallback are not proof of this session. Match caller ID, worktree and branch; inspect `entire session info <session-id> --json`. Require active state plus fresh lifecycle evidence from this caller during the current task before claiming live capture. An ID, installed hook file, trusted/discovered hook, old active record or historical checkpoint alone is insufficient. If freshness/source cannot be established without denied transcript access, mark live capture unverified. Never use `--transcript`, full/raw modes, denied transcript paths, or dump JSON metadata wholesale; project only safe IDs, paths, state, times, linkage and usage fields.

Conventional linked worktrees may discover the primary checkout's hook file rather than their own. Read ownership is not write ownership: compare the resolved discovered path, current-checkout path, project layer and trust. `worktree_path_not_discovered` may coexist with `ACTIVE (via root checkout)`; reconcile paths instead of blindly reinstalling. A branch lacking `.codex` can have a project-layer gap. Never copy/migrate hooks between worktrees or edit another checkout to resolve this.

## After meaningful authorized commits and pushes

Before an already-authorized commit, record original HEAD and bounded checkpoint ref identities. Let normal Git hooks perform capture; do not create a verification commit. Afterwards resolve the exact new SHA and extract only `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers (for example with Git's `%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)` format). Inspect metadata with `entire checkpoint explain --commit <exact-sha> --json` and `entire checkpoint list --session <exact-session-id> --json`; the latter is branch-scoped. Match exact commit, checkpoint and session IDs, including multi-session checkpoints. Never equate an empty branch-scoped list with deletion of all history. Missing linkage is a failure to verify, not a reason to amend the commit.

For git-refs storage, the checkpoint ref is `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last-two-ID-characters>/<id>`. Read the local ref SHA using Git; absence means local checkpoint unverified. Keep existing checkpoint refs intact, including legacy storage. Inspect selected metadata only; checkpoint trees contain private session content. Missing/null usage or incomplete child accounting is **unavailable**, not zero; report zero only if explicitly recorded.

Before an authorized push, establish the selected checkpoint destination and push_sessions setting from existing safe evidence. A normal code push can transmit transcript-derived checkpoint data; existing push authorization must cover that configured destination and content. If it does not, pause the push with the concrete missing scope. Never manually push shadow branches or change remotes/credentials. Afterwards compare each relevant local checkpoint ref SHA with the same exact ref returned by `git ls-remote --refs <approved-remote-name> <exact-ref>`; this is a remote read using existing access, not permission to authenticate anew. Bound runtime and output. If no safely established destination exists, report sync unknown. A local checkpoint, successful code push, cached origin ref or matching count alone does not prove checkpoint sync. Equal exact SHAs prove ref sync at observation time; dashboard linkage/ingestion requires separately observed session or commit view/API evidence. Don't gate this on Analytics.

## Handoff, weekly check and failures

Repeat the caller/linkage checks at handoff; an ended session with prior live evidence is valid handoff evidence, not currently active capture. Summarize repository/worktree, agent surface and binary version, session/resolution/state and freshness, original/current commit, checkpoint/local SHA, remote name/SHA and observation time, usage availability, dashboard evidence and outstanding boundary. Preserve evidence outside the repository only in an authorized location, excluding prompts and credentials.

If the surface is unsupported or capture is missing, give the exact boundary and smallest next step: e.g. discovered hooks but no caller state → an authorized fresh/resumed session in that worktree with reviewed hooks, then metadata verification. Continue authorized coding if appropriate, clearly marking capture unverified. Never relabel an import as live. For requested historical recovery, first inspect `entire import --help`, the agent-specific import help, and `entire session attach --help`; explain local-history versus commit-linkage effects and request the exact missing mutation permission before execution. # Entire continuity

This skill guides verification; loading it does not install or guarantee hooks. Check evidence in the actual agent session, binary and worktree. Keep live capture, historical import, local checkpoint linkage, remote ref sync and dashboard ingestion as separate findings. Aggregate Analytics is not session evidence; ignore the known Tailor Analytics discrepancy.

## Scope and authority

The maintained source is `.agents/skills/entire-continuity` in this repository. Use the copy tracked in the current checkout; older worktrees must integrate the approved source commit before expecting automatic discovery. Do not create global copies or cross-worktree symlinks.

Use existing authorization for ordinary task work. This skill alone authorizes no commits, pushes, imports, attachment, transcript uploads, scheduled checks or hidden automation. Weekly use means only an explicitly requested evidence review within this repository; it changes no approval rules and authorizes no autonomous check or schedule. Do not expand access or transmit credentials. Work only on the personal Mac; exclude StockGro and office projects.

Do not alter global Git config, authentication, hooks, trust records, permissions or credentials. Do not stop other sessions or repair dirty/diverged checkouts. Preserve checkpoint refs, original commit identities and other agents' work; never synthesize checkpoint trailers or claim retrospective live capture. Repairs need authorization for the concrete repair. Import/attach need explicit permission; attaching can amend HEAD, so permission to import is not permission to amend or force-push.

## Task-start preflight

1. Resolve the intended repository, checkout and shared Git directory with `git --no-optional-locks rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir`. Inspect `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v1 --branch`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD`, and upstream identity/divergence when present. Keep paths and SHA evidence; do not print file contents, remote URLs with embedded credentials, or full commit messages. A dirty checkout, detached HEAD, missing upstream or divergence is a finding, not permission to reset, stash, amend, fetch or switch branches. Existing upstream refs are cached evidence only.
2. Confirm Entire is already enabled from approved metadata or bounded settings inspection. If unrelated/unconfigured, report exclusion and stop this skill without enabling anything. In Tailor, inspect the existing worktree documentation when needed: `docs/entire-codex-worktrees.md` relative to the current checkout root. Never mutate that worktree or its branches as part of skill verification.
3. Run `entire version` and the actual session binary's `--version`; PATH Codex may differ from the desktop bundle. Verify syntax using installed `--help` and the matching tagged official docs. Reviewed baseline: Entire 0.11.4, desktop-bundled Codex 0.162.0-alpha.17.2, PATH Codex 0.153.4. Recheck after upgrades; the official integration tests pin Codex 0.149.0 and do not prove every newer surface works.
4. Check hook discovery, configured commands/timeouts, Git-hook wiring and trust separately from capture. Use already available status/doctor evidence or bounded approved inspection. `entire status --json` can reconcile exited sessions; `entire doctor </dev/null` is a noninteractive diagnostic, not a promise of zero state changes. Do not run either on shared live state when strict observation is required; report that diagnostic boundary instead. Never use `doctor --force`, enable/configure, run hook handlers manually, or fabricate trust hashes for verification. Review untrusted hooks through the user's Codex `/hooks` flow only when authorized.
5. Use `entire session current --json` (metadata only). Only `resolution` = `caller-env` or `ancestry` identifies the command's caller. Recent-worktree and `other-worktree` fallback are not proof of this session. Match caller ID, worktree and branch; inspect `entire session info <session-id> --json`. Require active state plus fresh lifecycle evidence from this caller during the current task before claiming live capture. An ID, installed hook file, trusted/discovered hook, old active record or historical checkpoint alone is insufficient. If freshness/source cannot be established without denied transcript access, mark live capture unverified. Never use `--transcript`, full/raw modes, denied transcript paths, or dump JSON metadata wholesale; project only safe IDs, paths, state, times, linkage and usage fields.

Conventional linked worktrees may discover the primary checkout's hook file rather than their own. Read ownership is not write ownership: compare the resolved discovered path, current-checkout path, project layer and trust. `worktree_path_not_discovered` may coexist with `ACTIVE (via root checkout)`; reconcile paths instead of blindly reinstalling. A branch lacking `.codex` can have a project-layer gap. Never copy/migrate hooks between worktrees or edit another checkout to resolve this.

## After meaningful authorized commits and pushes

Before an already-authorized commit, record original HEAD and bounded checkpoint ref identities. Let normal Git hooks perform capture; do not create a verification commit. Afterwards resolve the exact new SHA and extract only `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers (for example with Git's `%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)` format). Inspect metadata with `entire checkpoint explain --commit <exact-sha> --json` and `entire checkpoint list --session <exact-session-id> --json`; the latter is branch-scoped. Match exact commit, checkpoint and session IDs, including multi-session checkpoints. Never equate an empty branch-scoped list with deletion of all history. Missing linkage is a failure to verify, not a reason to amend the commit.

For git-refs storage, the checkpoint ref is `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last-two-ID-characters>/<id>`. Read the local ref SHA using Git; absence means local checkpoint unverified. Keep existing checkpoint refs intact, including legacy storage. Inspect selected metadata only; checkpoint trees contain private session content. Missing/null usage or incomplete child accounting is **unavailable**, not zero; report zero only if explicitly recorded.

Before an authorized push, establish the selected checkpoint destination and push_sessions setting from existing safe evidence. A normal code push can transmit transcript-derived checkpoint data; existing push authorization must cover that configured destination and content. If it does not, pause the push with the concrete missing scope. Never manually push shadow branches or change remotes/credentials. Afterwards compare each relevant local checkpoint ref SHA with the same exact ref returned by `git ls-remote --refs <approved-remote-name> <exact-ref>`; this is a remote read using existing access, not permission to authenticate anew. Bound runtime and output. If no safely established destination exists, report sync unknown. A local checkpoint, successful code push, cached origin ref or matching count alone does not prove checkpoint sync. Equal exact SHAs prove ref sync at observation time; dashboard linkage/ingestion requires separately observed session or commit view/API evidence. Don't gate this on Analytics.

## Handoff, weekly check and failures

Repeat the caller/linkage checks at handoff; an ended session with prior live evidence is valid handoff evidence, not currently active capture. Summarize repository/worktree, agent surface and binary version, session/resolution/state and freshness, original/current commit, checkpoint/local SHA, remote name/SHA and observation time, usage availability, dashboard evidence and outstanding boundary. Preserve evidence outside the repository only in an authorized location, excluding prompts and credentials.

If the surface is unsupported or capture is missing, give the exact boundary and smallest next step: e.g. discovered hooks but no caller state → an authorized fresh/resumed session in that worktree with reviewed hooks, then metadata verification. Continue authorized coding if appropriate, clearly marking capture unverified. Never relabel an import as live. For requested historical recovery, first inspect `entire import --help`, the agent-specific import help, and `entire session attach --help`; explain local-history versus commit-linkage effects and request the exact missing mutation permission before execution. No automatic amend, force, upload or live test commit.

Optional repeatability helper: `python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/classify_evidence.py <sanitized-evidence.json>`. Read its short input contract before use. It classifies manually normalized evidence, does not collect/verify facts, and performs no Git, Entire, network or transcript operations. Unknown facts stay unknown. For an explicitly requested weekly evidence review, invoke this skill and sample the week's exact authorized commits and checkpoints within the selected repository; report coverage limits, not universal completeness.

## Sources and known evidence

Use the [Entire 0.11.4 Codex integration contract](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/v0.11.4/cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/AGENT.md) for discovery/trust caveats and the [0.11.4 storage and remote reference](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/v0.11.4/README.md#checkpoint-remote) for sync behavior. Installed help governs executable syntax.

User-reported baseline, not this skill's new live test: bundled-CLI session `01a1287f-9b41-7ce2-86f4-d9384c3f8718`, checkpoint `01M4M835G024JZH0PJPA615GFB`, commit `381b750db363e4ff403cfdd3ac722455da00addb` on `codex/verify-entire-capture`; local/remote checkpoint SHA `6e35f68e8211412362beb43593473d950a03730b`. Eleven refs reportedly matched origin and dashboard commit linkage was observed. Session usage agreed across metadata/API/session view. Desktop UI live capture was not separately tested. Do not extrapolate these facts to the current session or investigate Analytics.

# Tailor

Tailor is a candidate project for neatHack (October 2026), currently under validation.

NIT-265 adds a bounded local Neatlogs replica: landing, fictional project entry, trace list, span details, tree and timeline. Every session contains two deterministic order lookup fixtures. Visitor text is saved; it does not generate personalization. No LLM or agent runs.

## Run the replica

Use Node >=26.7.0 and npm >=11.19.0 on the personal Mac.

```sh
npm ci
npx playwright install chromium # once, for browser tests
npm run dev
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:4321. The server binds loopback only. It deliberately does not load `.env.local` or use the Neatlogs key. Existing real SDK integration remains separate; do not mistake the replica fixtures for real Tailor execution telemetry.

For developer inspection and proposal validation, start the server with a local key, then use the same environment in another terminal:

```sh
export TAILOR_DEV_KEY="$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(require("node:crypto").randomBytes(32).toString("hex"))')"
npm run dev
# In a terminal with the same TAILOR_DEV_KEY:
npm run fixture -- validate
npm run fixture -- inspect
```

`validate` creates two fictional sessions, rejects a broken parent, verifies unchanged state, publishes a corrected supported fixture at v2, independently reads it back, rejects stale v1 and denies another session's read/write. `inspect` returns saved descriptions, scenario/version and canonical records; it requires the developer key. Never use real buyer input. `TAILOR_URL` selects another loopback port; `PORT` changes the server port; `TAILOR_DATA_PATH` changes the SQLite file.

Data lives in gitignored `.local/tailor.sqlite` with SQLite WAL/SHM sidecars. The directory is private (0700 when created); the persisted signing secret lets the browser's HttpOnly/SameSite cookie survive a server restart. A cookie grants one session only. A new session replaces that browser's cookie; older sessions remain available to authorized developer inspection. Full auth, sharing and retention policy are outside this local fictional proof. Nothing automatically expires from SQLite; manually reset after review, with the server stopped:

```sh
rm -f .local/tailor.sqlite .local/tailor.sqlite-wal .local/tailor.sqlite-shm
# Optional browser-test dataset reset, also with its server stopped:
rm -f .local/ui-test.sqlite .local/ui-test.sqlite-wal .local/ui-test.sqlite-shm
```

These commands destroy only the named local fictional datasets and invalidate their cookies; do not point the server at buyer data. No reset was applied to the primary checkout or another worktree.

## Checks

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run test:ui
npm run doctor:local
```

There is no lint script. Browser screenshots default to `test-results/evidence`; set `TAILOR_SCREENSHOT_DIR` to a review folder to preserve them. Tests use disposable fictional data, local request interruption/failure simulation and a test-only developer key. The HTTP tests close/reopen the database/server to verify restart persistence, full-document rollback, concurrent CAS conflicts and cross-session denial.

`doctor:probe`, `env:check` and `smoke:trace` retain their existing meanings in AGENTS.md. Authenticated probing and synthetic real trace ingestion were not run for NIT-265 because the real account is read-only for this task. `neatlogs` remains pinned to 1.1.28. `npm audit` reports 10 moderate and 4 high advisories in its existing SDK/OpenTelemetry/protobuf dependency chain; this slice does not upgrade that integration.

## API contract

Types live in `src/contracts.ts`; all UI projections originate in the session's single canonical dataset. Cookies and developer keys are never embedded in frontend code. Every response is `no-store`. Errors are `{ error: { code, message } }`.

| Method/path | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| POST `/api/sessions` | `{description, scenario}` plus `Idempotency-Key` (16–80 alphanumeric/hyphen characters); 201 session + HttpOnly cookie. Exact retries return the original session; conflicting input returns 409. |
| GET `/api/session` | Current browser's canonical session. |
| GET `/api/sessions/:id` | Cookie-owned canonical session including saved description, version and active fixture. |
| GET `/api/sessions/:id/traces` | `{version, activeScenario, total, filtered, traces}`. Supports `q`, `scenario`, `detection=yes/no`, `tag`, `minMs`, `maxMs`. Search is case-insensitive canonical JSON substring; latency uses milliseconds. |
| GET `/api/sessions/:id/traces/:traceId` | `{version, trace}` including flat parent-linked spans, I/O, errors and timing. |
| GET `/api/sessions/:id/traces/:traceId/spans/:spanId` | `{version, span}`. |
| GET `/api/dev/sessions` | Developer key header `x-tailor-dev-key`; inspect all saved local fictional sessions. |
| POST `/api/dev/sessions/:id/proposal` | Developer key AND owning cookie. `{expectedVersion, dataset}`; 200 accepted canonical session. Only exact supported fixtures with either active scenario validate. Immutable ownership/input/IDs; no arbitrary personalization. |

Transactions publish a complete validated document or nothing. Invalid fixture 422, stale version 409, unknown/cross-session ID 404, missing developer key 403, unsupported method 405, unsupported filter 400, malformed JSON 400, content type 415 and >32KB body 413. Disconnects retain the last accepted version. Supported browser URLs are `/demo/:id/traces`, `/demo/:id/traces/:traceId` and detail `?span=:spanId`.

See [reference and deviation notes](docs/nit-265-reference.md) for current-product observations and review boundaries.

## Local history

`setup/local` records the tracing setup at `c7b80e7ea3f5a9f08d306303d11ce08b379ffe98`. The next commit on that branch carries an Entire checkpoint trailer that does not resolve. This recovery branch starts from the setup commit, so that trailer is not part of this history.
